title: Silas and the Safehouse
premise: Marguerite Kavanagh, a fixer for an embassy that exists on no map, receives a meeting invitation from her handler — sent twelve hours after his death. The summons pulls her into a trap set by factions inside her own service, all converging on a Russian defector who may be the bait in someone else's game. With the summit forty-eight hours away and her only ally a defector she cannot trust, Marguerite must choose between the rules that kept her alive and the truth that could burn everything down. In the end, she delivers the defector to the summit — but exposes the conspiracy herself, trading her career, her cover, and any hope of going home for the one clean act left to her.
about_author: August Iversen is the pen name of a former intelligence-adjacent analyst who now writes thrillers from a farmhouse in rural Norway. Their work is known for procedural precision, morally compromised protagonists, and endings that cost the hero something real.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A dead handler's calendar invite appears on her secure terminal, scheduled for tomorrow at a safehouse she helped decommission years ago. Against protocol, she goes, finding the defector Anton Voss waiting instead of her handler — and a kill team arriving minutes behind him. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into instinct as fifteen years of trust in the system collapses in a single night.

chapters.title: Rules of Extraction
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Marguerite and Voss. On the run through Vienna, they piece together that Voss carries proof a faction inside the service orchestrated the handler's death to control the summit's outcome. Marguerite's duty says deliver him; her gut says he's the bait. Emotional beat: wary intimacy — two liars learning each other's tells while every contact they reach turns up dead or turned.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Voss's POV, then Marguerite's. Cornered at a border crossing, Voss confesses his defection was brokered by the very conspirators hunting them — he is the lure, knowingly or not. Marguerite realizes her own extraction orders were written to end with both their deaths. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve; love against duty crystallizes as she burns her identity to buy them one clean path to the summit.

chapters.title: What the Summit Was For
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She walks Voss into the summit as ordered — then detonates the conspiracy publicly, broadcasting the evidence to every delegation present and accepting arrest as the price. The corrupt faction falls; Voss testifies; Marguerite survives, stripped of name and service. Emotional beat: costly catharsis — survival finally means something because she stopped paying everyone else's price and paid her own.
